sessions.title: Distinguish locality, street, building and apartment marks

steps.title: Recognize the locality mark
steps.body: In 115114 г. Москва, г. marks the city or locality; the supplied English gloss is city. The number is a postcode, not the abbreviation being tested. The options street and building refer to different components. Read the requested abbreviation rather than treating every number or place name as the same part of an address.

steps.title: Distinguish street, building and apartment
steps.body: In ул. Петрова, д. 14, кв. 15, the first mark ул. identifies the street. The later д. identifies the building, and кв. identifies the apartment. The supplied line thus separates street name, building number and apartment number. The answer street matches the first mark; city belongs to the locality mark and apartment belongs to the later mark. Abbreviations label address components; their positions and associated numbers help distinguish them.

steps.title: Identify a building mark without inventing delivery details
steps.body: The separate supplied mark д. has the English gloss building. It does not name the city or street. sessions.title: Distinguish specific unknown, open and speaker-known reference

steps.title: A specific person whose identity is unknown
steps.body: В доме действительно кто-то был means that someone really was in the house. The label референтность и неизвестность говорящему describes reference to a particular person whose identity is unknown to the speaker in this supplied use. It does not mean nobody was there. Referential concerns whether a particular entity is intended; it is different from whether the speaker knows that entity's identity.

steps.title: An unspecified alternative is not absence
steps.body: куда-нибудь is the supplied example of an open, unspecified destination. The label являются нереферентными means non-referential in this classification: no particular fixed destination is selected. An alternative is considered against other possible destinations, as in a future plan, desire or conditional context. This is not the label референтность и неизвестность говорящему for a particular unknown entity, nor референтный денотативный статус слабой определённости for a specific entity known to the speaker. The classification concerns this supplied series/use, not a universal translation of every indefinite form.

steps.title: A specific choice known to the speaker, with overlap limits
steps.body: кое-какие is classified as референтный денотативный статус слабой определённости: weakly definite reference to particular things known to the speaker but not assumed known to the listener. It differs from a particular unknown entity and from an open alternative with no fixed referent. The retained rule Местоимение на -то может употребляться также и в значении местоимения на -нибудь says the first series can also be used with the meaning of the second in some contexts. Do not infer a rigid one-suffix/one-meaning division. These checks classify the supplied forms; broader production and selection need the sentence and discourse context.

sessions.title: Apply a supplied letter framework without universal style rules

steps.title: Organize the supplied problem-and-request letter
steps.body: In this lesson's problem-and-request model, state the reason, explain relevant facts, then make the request. For a letter explaining a problem and requesting action, this sequence gives the recipient a reason and relevant support for the request. It is a supplied framework, not a rule that every Russian letter must put its main point last. English and Russian letters have different genres and purposes; a source's contrast is not a universal rule for either language.

steps.title: Distinguish the greeting, body and closing
steps.body: Здравствуйте! is a greeting, not a rule about how close the recipient is. The retained example glosses it as Greetings. Уважаемый Иван Иванович is another supplied address formula, glossed Respected Ivan Ivanovich. Select address wording for the recipient, relationship and genre; the English word dear is not a universal ban determined by this neutral greeting. The claim every unfamiliar recipient forbids any greeting translated as dear overgeneralizes from one greeting to every addressee. In the supplied layout, Sender’s address and date precedes the Greeting, then comes the Body, followed by Closing and signature. A greeting starts the address to the reader; the body carries the message; the closing and signature end the letter. The framework is not mandatory for every letter or electronic message.

steps.title: Read what happened to the described entity
steps.body: A past passive participle describes an entity affected by an action. The supplied form сде́ланный has the meaning done/made. The form напи́санный means written, and уби́тый means killed. These words describe what was done to the entity; they do not identify it as the person doing the action. The three supplied meanings differ by the underlying action. Choosing written for сде́ланный would replace doing or making with writing; choosing killed would replace it with killing.

steps.title: Recognize the supplied long forms without inventing a universal algorithm
steps.body: The retained examples are long past passive forms with adjective-type endings. In the shown сде́ланный and напи́санный forms, the formation contains double n; уби́тый has t. The retained source shows these forms from perfective verbs. This lesson recognizes the supplied forms; these endings alone are not a complete productive formation rule for every verb. Broader formation includes other suffix patterns and lexical restrictions, so do not manufacture an unlisted form from this small set. An imperfective past passive can exist; the supplied perfective examples are not a universal claim that every past passive must come from a perfective verb.

steps.title: Distinguish the action meaning from long versus short form
steps.body: The meaning written belongs to напи́санный, not to the doing/making form сде́ланный or the killing form уби́тый. The meaning killed belongs to уби́тый, not to the other two actions. The retained short form напи́сан has a single n and lacks the long adjective ending shown in напи́санный. Long versus short form is different from the action meaning: both writing forms concern writing. These checks select the action meaning of a supplied form; they do not test production of all short-form gender and number endings.

steps.title: Identify the writer in the retained passive sentence
steps.body: письмо написано Иваном — the letter was written by Ivan. The letter is the entity affected by the writing; Ivan is the writer identified in the retained sentence. The passive form describes the letter’s state or result, rather than saying that the letter writes somebody. The short passive form in the sentence differs from the long headword напи́санный. A longer sentence supplies context that a headword lacks; do not infer a writer, reader or exact time from a bare participle alone. Active participles are outside this required Unit27 lesson.

steps.title: Meaning differs between a passive description, a finite verb and an infinitive
steps.body: The supplied обсужда́емый has the meaning being discussed. It describes something affected by discussion, rather than naming the person doing the discussing. The source also permits an able-to-be-discussed reading; the checked English option here is being discussed. The supporting verb form оставля́ем means we leave: it is a first-person plural present-tense form, with we performing the action, not a passive description. The infinitive оставля́ть means to leave and does not by itself name a we subject. Choose we leave for the finite form and to leave for the infinitive. The option to discuss is an infinitive meaning rather than the checked passive description. Different action meanings and grammatical functions must not be exchanged simply because forms share a stem.

sessions.title: Read the described letter, writer and separate main action

steps.title: Separate the letter description from the sentence action
steps.body: Письмо, написанное Анной, лежит на столе. means the letter Anna wrote is on the table. The participial phrase написанное Анной describes the letter: written is the action affecting it, and Anna is the named writer. The main statement locates the letter on the table. Being written and being on the table are separate parts of the reading. Neither the table nor the letter is the writer. The sentence does not say that Anna put the letter away, and the writer is not identified as its reader. A passive participle describes the affected entity; an agent phrase can name the person responsible for that particular action.

steps.title: Do not transfer the main-action subject to an unnamed participle agent
steps.body: Анна убрала прочитанное письмо. means Anna put away the letter that had been read. Anna performs the putting-away action; the description прочитанное письмо says that the letter had already been read. The sentence does not name the reader. Anna might or might not have read it; neither reading can be asserted from this sentence alone. Already read is different from just written or still reading aloud. The supplied passive description expresses the completed reading of the letter, not an ongoing action by Anna. Recognize the main verb, the affected letter and any explicitly named agent separately. These checks interpret the supplied readings; accent placement alone cannot answer who wrote or read the letter, and recognizing these examples does not demonstrate production of an unfamiliar participial sentence.

sessions.title: Choose the time relationship the source states for imperfective adverbial forms

steps.title: Read two actions happening together
steps.body: An imperfective verbal adverb describes an accompanying action. In the supplied читая письмо, он улыбался, he was reading the letter while he smiled. Reading and smiling overlap: simultaneous means during the same interval as the main predicate. The main verb places this example in the past; читая does not independently mean absolute present time. The retained examples думая and учась illustrate imperfective verbal-adverb forms. An isolated form cannot establish the tense of an absent main verb.

steps.title: Keep the two actions with the same person
steps.body: In читая письмо, он улыбался, The pronoun he is the explicit main-clause subject. The reader and the person smiling are the same person. The verbal adverb supplies an accompanying action by that subject, not an action by a second unrelated person. Identify the main verb and its subject before deciding who performs the accompanying action. These checks recognize timing and shared subject in the supplied construction; they do not demonstrate forming an unfamiliar verbal adverb or judging every possible literary use.

steps.title: Read the completed action before the main action
steps.body: A perfective verbal adverb normally presents an action completed before the main action in this taught construction. Anterior means earlier relative to that action. The retained сказав and научившись illustrate these forms; their labels alone do not fix an absolute past tense. Read the accompanying main predicate to establish the sentence time.

steps.title: Earlier does not necessarily mean past
steps.body: In написав письмо, она отправит его завтра, she will send the letter tomorrow after writing it. The writing precedes the future sending: anterior to a future main action is the matching description. The sentence does not require the writing to have happened before the present moment. The pronoun she names the main subject, and the writer and sender are the same person. An absolute present label loses the relative timing; assigning a different subject loses the supplied construction.

This small example set supplies recognition practice, not a complete productive algorithm for unlisted verbs.

sessions.title: Choose the admitted time label for the shown active form

steps.title: Distinguish active past and present descriptions
steps.body: An active participle describes an entity performing the action. The retained чита́вшая is the past reading form; чита́ющая is the present reading form. The labels in the past and in the present distinguish these supplied forms. They do not identify a passive entity being read. An English description of reading can express the action without itself specifying this past/present contrast.

steps.title: Read the question as well as the form
steps.body: For чита́ющая, select in the present when asked for its time label. For чита́вшая, select in the past for its own time label. Classify the displayed form itself. Selecting the other time label would test following a reversal instruction rather than interpreting the participle. The gloss that read gives an action meaning rather than the requested time classification.

steps.title: Recognize the separate living example
steps.body: The retained живу́щие means living. In the supplied example, people perform the living action; this is an active present participle. sessions.title: Distinguish admitted long, short and invariant adjective forms

steps.title: Recognize the long and short forms
steps.body: The retained но́вый and нов both mean new. The first is the long form and the second is the masculine singular short form. The grammatical check asks which form is shown, rather than its English gloss. Long adjectives have case, gender and number inflection; short adjectives vary for gender and number, not case. The retained examples are recognition targets, not a universal rule for producing short forms by removing endings.

steps.title: Distinguish a predicate from a noun description
steps.body: In the taught modern use, short adjectives occur only in the nominative and are used predicatively to describe their subject. A long adjective can modify a noun attributively and can also be a predicate. The choice depends on the sentence, not a universal rule about one fixed word position. The following supplied forms, complete clauses and noun phrases support bounded agreement and function checks; they do not settle every long-versus-short semantic or stylistic choice.

steps.title: A short-looking word need not be a short adjective
steps.body: The retained беж means beige and is an invariant colour form, unchanged for case, gender and number. Its short appearance does not make it the short counterpart of но́вый. Keep lexical meaning, inflection and adjective function separate. The correct glosses remain in Vocabulary Lab as word-meaning practice; they do not satisfy the independent adjective grammar checks.

steps.title: Apply short-form gender and number agreement
steps.body: The supplied short forms of new are нов for masculine singular, нова́ for feminine singular, но́во for neuter singular and новы́ for plural. Short adjectives agree with their subject in gender and number; they do not have a modern case paradigm. In the retained noun examples, книга is feminine singular, письмо is neuter singular, and книги has the supplied plural reading. Choose the short form for that subject rather than another form with the same lexical meaning. Some adjectives lack short forms and stress can change; these supplied forms are not a universal truncation recipe.

steps.title: A long form can be a predicate
steps.body: The complete clauses Поезд старый and Студент новый say that the train is old and the student is new. Their long adjectives predicate a property of the subject. sessions.title: Decide comma boundaries in the supplied participial constructions

steps.title: A following descriptive phrase is set off on both sides
steps.body: In Программа, написанная в спешке, выполнила недопустимую операцию. The phrase describing the program follows its noun and is set off by commas on both sides. The retained label выделяется запятыми с двух сторон names that treatment. A single comma before the phrase would omit its closing boundary in this supplied sentence.

steps.title: Compare the phrase placed before its noun
steps.body: In Написанная в спешке программа выполнила недопустимую операцию. The same descriptive phrase precedes the noun. The supplied example has no separating commas: запятые не ставятся is its label. Phrase position helps distinguish these two examples; this does not mean commas are never used before a described noun.

steps.title: Apply the pronoun and cause exceptions
steps.body: The retained rule states exceptions when the described entity is a personal pronoun or the participial phrase expresses a cause. Воспитанный в традициях Фоппы, Бернардо Дзенале и Амброджо Бергоньоне, он прошёл обучение в мастерской Леонардо. The opening phrase describes он, so A separating comma follows the opening participial phrase before the main clause. The comma after Фоппы is internal to the list of names. The later comma after Бергоньоне marks the modifier boundary before он; do not treat every visible comma as a modifier boundary. Изумлённый этим хохотом, Павел сел на пол и смотрел куда-то в угол The retained source row explicitly gives this example a causal shade, so A separating comma follows the opening participial phrase before the main clause. The ordinary preceding-noun label запятые не ставятся cannot cancel these exceptions. The optional source wording личным местоимением and кроме тех случаев identifies a category/connective, not a complete comma decision; its reference question does not satisfy these language checks.

steps.title: Check the continuing clause and sentence end
steps.body: Туча, нависшая над высокими вершинами тополей, уже сыпала дождиком The phrase describes Туча and is followed by the continuing predicate, so Separating commas mark both boundaries of the participial phrase before the sentence continues. Вдали виднеется маяк, стоящий у моря Here the phrase describes маяк and ends the supplied construction, so A separating comma precedes the terminal participial phrase, with no closing comma at sentence end. A closing separating comma would have no continuing clause after it. By contrast, No separating comma is used between the participial phrase and the word it describes. is the ordinary non-causal, non-pronoun preceding-noun default shown in the earlier program example. These are bounded supplied constructions; not every phrase before a noun needs a comma and not every phrase after a word fits one universal rule.

steps.title: Follow the actor and the order of actions
steps.body: In Закончив письмо, Анна пошла на почту и отправила его., Anna finishes the letter before going to the post office and sending it. Anna performs the actions; the letter does not travel alone and the post office does not write it. The finishing phrase belongs before the departure, not after the sending. Read the entire supplied passage when a check shows only a fragment.

steps.title: Resolve the final action without substituting a register answer
steps.body: The supplied отправила его means she sent it, with the letter as the object in this passage. The passage places the sending after Anna goes to the post office. It does not say that she stayed at the table, finished at the market, left the letter at home or received a letter at home. Those alternatives replace a stated event or location. Bookish register classification is a separate objective and cannot answer who acted, where she went or what she did with the letter.

sessions.title: Answer from the admitted capstone story

steps.title: Follow the rescue before the second return
steps.body: In the retained story a woman reports that a two-year-old girl remains in the burning house. Bob, the dog sent by the firefighters, returns carrying the girl. The supplied нёс де́вочку belongs to that rescue, before the later discovery involving a doll. The mother is glad her daughter is alive; the passage does not describe the rescue itself as the comic discovery.

steps.title: Connect the laughter to what the dog carries next
steps.body: After the rescue Bob goes back into the house and returns carrying a large doll, expressed by несла́ большу́ю ку́клу. When the people recognize it, все расхохота́лись describes their laughter. The female grammatical form refers to the dog in that part of the narration, not the rescued girl carrying the doll. provenanceRecords.sourceRecordId: future:In English, when reporting a story, we usually change the tense of what was said
provenanceRecords.shippedText: In English, when reporting a story, we usually change the tense of what was said: compare "I ''am'' English" with "He said he ''was'' English" - the reported verb changes tense. In Russian, however, we keep the tense the same, so the same report is literally, "He said he '''is''' English" - "'''Он сказа́л, что он англича́нин'''", not "'''Он сказа́л, что он ''был'' англича́нином'''".

provenanceRecords.shippedText:
In Russia, dates are usually written in "day month year" (DMY) order. This order is used in both the all-numeric date (for example "28.08.17") and the expanded form (for example "28 августа 2017 г."); the trailing "г" is short for "года" (goda, "of the year"). Coincidentally, in Polish the word for year is "rok", so a similar date format is used by the Poles e.g. 1987r). Single-digit numbers for day or month may have a preceding zero (for example "28.08.2017") is more usual.

When saying the date, it is usually pronounced using the ordinal number of the day first (in neutral grammatical gender), then the month in genitive case (for example "Двадцать восьмое августа").

The complete home-delivery organization names the recipient, then the street with the house and any apartment or office, then the locality, then the district, oblast, krai, or republic when that unit applies, then the country, then the postcode. The sentence determines the case; absence meaning alone does not. There is no nominative form in this negative paradigm.

Наш means our; Ваш means your. In the worked phrase на́ша сестра́, both words are feminine singular nominative. Possessives such as мо́й and тво́й agree with the noun they describe in gender, number and case. Choose the form from the noun, not from the gender of its owner. Start with the nominative forms below, then compare the feminine accusative example.

In мой стол, стол is masculine singular. In моя собака, собака is feminine singular. Both phrases mean my plus a noun, but the Russian form of my changes to match the noun.

In the nominative singular, мо́й is masculine and моя́ is feminine. For стол choose мо́й; for собака choose моя́. The form follows the noun being described.

моё is the neuter singular nominative form of my. мои́ is the plural nominative form. A singular noun does not take the plural form in these choices.

Наш means our; Ваш means your. In the worked phrase на́ша сестра́, both words are feminine singular nominative. To put this phrase in the direct-object accusative, change both words: на́ша сестра́ becomes на́шу сестру́. Keep the same noun and feminine singular agreement. на́шего бра́та changes the referent, and на́ши is plural.

тво́й is masculine singular nominative; твоя́ is feminine singular nominative. Both mean your. To change the masculine form to the feminine form while keeping nominative singular, choose твоя́.

After ж, ц, ч, ш, or щ, an unstressed о in an ending is written е. That replacement is not a rule for every unstressed о. In хоро́шее, the unstressed ending after ш uses е. The и in хоро́шие follows a different spelling condition: write и rather than ы after ш. Spelling limits the letters in an ending; gender, number and case determine which form is needed.

Adjectives agree with their nouns in gender, number and case. In хорошее письмо, the adjective describes a neuter singular noun. хоро́ший is the dictionary form: masculine singular nominative. This lesson compares singular and plural nominative forms, then explains the spelling in the retained plurals.

After г, к, х, ж, ч, ш, or щ, write и rather than ы. The seven-letter condition is required. This rule applies to the spelling of noun and adjective endings. In кни́ги, и follows г; in хоро́шие, и follows ш. The rule controls spelling, but the question determines the required gender, number and case.

For these nominative checks, кни́га means book in the singular and кни́ги means books in the plural. To form this plural, replace the singular ending with the plural ending: кни́га becomes кни́ги. The stem ends in г, so the seven-letter rule requires и. To return to singular nominative, choose кни́га.

кни́ги is plural nominative in this lesson. дни is also plural nominative and means days. Its и does not follow a letter in the seven-letter set, so дни is not an example of that spelling replacement. Not every plural ending in и comes from the seven-letter rule. Identify number from the requested form and context.

For the masculine singular dictionary form, choose хоро́ший. All these options are correctly spelled: the questions test form recognition rather than choosing between correct and incorrect spellings.

Aspect describes how an action is viewed, not when it happens. Imperfective can focus on an activity, repetition, or the fact that an action occurred without emphasizing its endpoint. Perfective presents an event with its boundary or result. Imperfective does not by itself mean unfinished. говори́ть is imperfective; сказа́ть is perfective. These infinitives do not specify tense on their own.

Many Russian verbs are learned in an aspect pair, but not every verb has two words, and a pair is not automatic. говорить and сказать are context-dependent counterparts, not a universal pair for the English verb speak. For the saying/telling pair shown here, the perfective counterpart of говори́ть is сказа́ть; the imperfective counterpart of сказа́ть is говори́ть. These checks ask you to recognize this vocabulary pair, not choose aspect in a sentence.

Aspect describes how an action is viewed, not when it happens. Imperfective can focus on an activity, repetition, or the fact that an action occurred without emphasizing its endpoint. Perfective presents an event with its boundary or result. Imperfective does not by itself mean unfinished. говори́ть is imperfective; сказа́ть is perfective. These infinitives do not specify tense on their own.

Many Russian verbs are learned in an aspect pair, but not every verb has two words, and a pair is not automatic. говорить and сказать are context-dependent counterparts, not a universal pair for the English verb speak. For the saying/telling pair shown here, the perfective counterpart of говори́ть is сказа́ть; the imperfective counterpart of сказа́ть is говори́ть. These checks ask you to recognize this vocabulary pair, not choose aspect in a sentence.

де́лать is imperfective; сде́лать is perfective. Both concern doing or making. The perfective focuses on accomplishing the action; the imperfective can describe the activity or its occurrence without that focus. Given де́лать and a request for its perfective counterpart, choose сде́лать. говори́ть concerns speaking or saying and belongs to the other pair. Learn the shown pair rather than assuming every prefix changes only aspect.

The instrumental singular -ом fits the hard stem of the relevant noun class. Soft stems use their own instrumental ending, so -ом is not universal. Here, keep the stem of сто́л and add -ом to obtain столо́м. Learn the stress with the whole form.

Instrumental plural refers to more than one. кни́га is the dictionary singular form for book; кни́гами is instrumental plural. Keep the stem and use -ами in this pattern. Given an instrumental plural request, choose кни́гами.

Instrumental plural nouns commonly use -ами or -ями, with exceptions. The book, house and table forms shown here use -ами. This is a noun ending; adjectives have their own agreement endings. These checks ask you to recognize the displayed pattern, not derive every noun form.

кни́гам is dative plural; кни́гах is prepositional plural. Neither is instrumental plural. Compare their endings with кни́гами: the final vowel is part of the instrumental plural ending here.

до́м names a house in the dictionary singular. дома́ми is instrumental plural. For this plural case request choose дома́ми, including the stress shown in the retained form.

дома́м is dative plural. до́мом is instrumental singular. The first has the wrong case; the second has the right case but the wrong number for an instrumental plural request. дома́ми meets both requirements.

сто́л is the dictionary singular form for table. стола́ми is instrumental plural. For an instrumental plural request, select стола́ми and learn its stress with the ending.

стола́м is dative plural; столо́м is instrumental singular. Neither meets both parts of an instrumental plural request. стола́ми supplies instrumental case and plural number together.

Я написал хорошим новым карандашом — I wrote with a good new pencil. The pencil is the tool used for writing: this is the means instrumental, without a preposition before the tool phrase. Я хочу встречу с интересной русской женщиной — I want a meeting with an interesting Russian woman. Here with introduces the person involved in the meeting: this is the accompaniment line, using a preposition followed by instrumental forms.

For a means instrumental request, choose the writing sentence because its pencil is the instrument. For an accompaniment line request, choose the meeting sentence because it describes being with a person. English with can express both roles; its presence alone does not decide which Russian construction is used. Read what the phrase contributes to the event.

The same preposition can govern different cases in different uses. For the preposition meaning under, instrumental describes location, while accusative can describe a destination under something. Movement within a location does not by itself require accusative: distinguish where something is from where it is going. These isolated-word checks contain no movement context and therefore do not assess that case choice.

над — over. под — under. These spatial meanings contrast vertical positions. The over label belongs to the first preposition; the under label belongs to the second. In a location construction, both can govern instrumental forms. The questions here recognize meanings from isolated prepositions; they do not ask you to choose a noun ending.

The same preposition can govern different cases in different uses. For the preposition meaning under, instrumental describes location, while accusative can describe a destination under something. Movement within a location does not by itself require accusative: distinguish where something is from where it is going. These isolated-word checks contain no movement context and therefore do not assess that case choice.

перед — before. между — between. In the spatial use introduced here, before means in front of; it is not a universal translation for every English time expression with before. Between places something relative to two things. When choosing a displayed English label, compare the specific spatial meaning, including the alternative behind. Learn the meaning first; sentence use still requires the appropriate case.

For the first form choose to become. For the second form choose remain among the displayed choices. The English past-tense word became does not correctly label either infinitive.

An instrumental complement can describe the role or state of the subject after a linking verb, rather than an instrument used to carry out an action. The verbs shown in this lesson can occur in that construction. These checks show only the verbs and ask for their meanings. Recognizing a verb meaning is a first step; it does not demonstrate forming a complete sentence with an instrumental complement.

казаться — appear to be. оказаться — turn out to be. The first concerns how something seems; the second concerns what it proves to be. Work the second choice by selecting turn out to be, rather than the meaning of continuation. A displayed infinitive still does not specify a past event. Keep these meanings distinct from becoming and remaining.

пе́рвый — first. второ́й — second. тре́тий — third. четвёртый — fourth. An ordinal identifies position in an ordered sequence; a cardinal tells how many. These isolated ordinal forms are masculine nominative singular. Learn the position expressed by each form before choosing it.

Ordinals agree with their noun in gender, number and case, like adjectives. восемнадцатую девушку means the eighteenth girl as a feminine accusative noun phrase. The retained example comes from a sentence about photographing her; this displayed fragment alone does not mean She just photographed. The ordinal ending follows the noun phrase, rather than staying in the masculine dictionary form. These recognition checks do not assess producing agreement in a sentence.

For the first ordinal, choose пе́рвый; for the second ordinal, choose второ́й; for the third ordinal, choose тре́тий. четвёртый expresses fourth, so it fails each of those requests. Read the English request: the separately shown Russian cue may name a different position and is not the target to copy.

одна минута — one minute. две минуты — two minutes. пять минут — five minutes. The noun for minute is feminine, so one and two use feminine forms here. Compare the masculine hour and year phrases. The noun is nominative singular after one, genitive singular after two, and genitive plural after five.

For basic nominative or inanimate accusative counts, an ending of 1 follows the one-minute pattern, endings 2, 3 or 4 follow the two-minute pattern, and endings 0 or 5 through 9 follow the five-minute pattern. Endings 11 through 14 take the five-minute pattern instead of following the final digit alone. Different case constructions require additional numeral and noun changes.

For a one-minute row, choose одна минута. For a two-minute row, choose две минуты. For a five-minute row, choose пять минут. Each other phrase names a different quantity. Январь — January. Февраль — February. Март — March. Апрель — April. These vocabulary labels name months, not complete dates. Read the shown Russian word and select its matching English month.

Июнь — June. Июль — July. Август — August. Декабрь — December. June and July have similar Russian spellings but differ in the consonant before the final soft sign. December names the final month of the year. These retained forms include the later check targets and their competing alternatives; this selected set is not a complete twelve-month production lesson.

Month names normally use lowercase within a Russian sentence. These retained vocabulary labels begin with capitals; that presentation is not a rule to capitalize every month name. For Июнь select June, and for Декабрь select December. Knowing the standalone name does not demonstrate forming a full date: a month in a date can have a different case form. Learn those constructions separately.

Который час? — What time is it? This fixed question asks for the current clock time. The noun час normally means hour; its retained example label time reflects this question context rather than a universal translation of the isolated noun. Learn the complete question as a unit.

A current-time question and the time when an event happens are different requests. The retained event sentences use at-time expressions. A preposition introduces several of them, while the without construction expresses minutes remaining until the upcoming hour. Study the complete source examples before selecting their readings.

Концерт начинается в шесть часов. — 18.00. Она была дома в час. — 13.00. These are the readings assigned by the retained source. The bare six-hour and one-hour expressions do not themselves distinguish evening from morning; the source readings depend on context. Do not infer that every occurrence of six means eighteen.

красне́е — redder. бо́лее до́брый — kinder. The first is a short comparative with an ending expressing a higher degree of redness; this short form does not change for gender, number or case. This retained English rendering accompanies an imperfective form describing motion toward the friend; the Russian form alone does not specify how long he was on the way. The distractor he was already on the way for a long time adds duration that is not supplied, and he refused to go contradicts the setting-out sentence.

Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца — The boy stepped back from the stranger. The verb and the phrase after it express movement away from the stranger. There is no additional relative clause in this displayed sentence. Они у́летят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Мяч залетел на крышу дома. — The ball flew onto the roof of the house. These are different subjects and paths. The prefix contributes to the motion meaning, while the accompanying phrases identify the path and time; do not substitute a translation of a different example.

The reflexive possessive refers to the subject as the owner. Its gender, number and case agree with the possessed noun, not with the owner. The retained dictionary forms are свой, своя, своё and свои. A masculine owner and a feminine owner can therefore use the same possessive form with the same noun.

The reflexive possessive refers to the subject as the owner. Its gender, number and case agree with the possessed noun, not with the owner. The retained dictionary forms are свой, своя, своё and свои. A masculine owner and a feminine owner can therefore use the same possessive form with the same noun.

Бо́ря рассказа́л о своём люби́мом фи́льме. — (Borya told about his favorite movie.). А́нна рассказа́ла о своём люби́мом фи́льме. — (Anna told about her favorite movie.). In each sentence the favorite movie belongs to the subject. The movie noun has the same gender, number and case in both, so the possessive form stays the same. The name and past-verb agreement change. The exercise asks you to preserve that movie object while changing the subject.

Анна прочитала статью за два часа. — the article was finished within two hours. Here the perfective reading verb and the completion-time construction present the article as finished within the two-hour period. Contrast that with time spent reading without asserting completion. This completion interval differs from the forward-looking time until the Latvia journey. кто — никто́. что — ничто́. The first pair concerns a person and nobody; the second concerns a thing and nothing. The indefinite options не́кто and не́что refer to an unspecified person or thing, not the corresponding nobody/nothing form. Do not treat a similar-looking prefix as proof of the same meaning.

Negative predicative constructions express the absence of a person or thing for an action. The construction selects a case form; it has no nominative form. Compare the indefinite pronoun separately. не́кого спросить — there is nobody to ask. This is absence of a person available for the infinitive action; it differs from an unspecified person and from there is nothing to ask.

не́кто is an indefinite pronoun, a person whose identity is not specified. It is not the predicative negative of кто. Absence of a person uses a case form: не́кого has the same form in the genitive and accusative, while не́кому is dative and не́кем instrumental. The sentence determines the case; absence meaning alone does not. There is no nominative form in this negative paradigm. The current checks recognize the absence meaning; they do not uniquely identify genitive from the shared genitive/accusative form.

provenanceRecords.shippedText: В доме действительно кто-то был means that someone really was in the house. The label референтность и неизвестность говорящему describes reference to a particular person whose identity is unknown to the speaker in this supplied use. It does not mean nobody was there. Referential concerns whether a particular entity is intended; it is different from whether the speaker knows that entity's identity.

Distinguish polite singular address from grammatical plural shape

provenanceRecords.shippedText: The retained grammar note describes polite address to one person using forms shared with the plural. In personal letters and official papers, a capital initial can mark respectful address to one recipient. This written convention is different from plural meaning. The same grammatical forms can address several people, so a capital initial alone does not establish the number of addressees. Identify the recipient from context, not from the English label plural form.

Keep capitalization tied to written context

provenanceRecords.shippedText: In the supplied respectful written-address convention, Вы, Вас and Вам have capital initials. Current Gramota guidance distinguishes respectful address to one recipient from address to several people or a general audience, where lowercase is used. A sentence-initial capital is also ordinary sentence capitalization and need not mark respectful singular address. Lowercase outside this convention is not automatically rude. Capitalization cannot be heard in speech. These checks recognize the shown letter case; choosing forms for a new letter requires recipient and genre context.

Separate an enclosure from a closing

provenanceRecords.shippedText: The retained pair к настоящему письму прилагается — enclosed please find introduces something supplied with the letter. The English gloss is a conventional correspondence expression, not a complete list of possible translations. It has an enclosure function. С уважением — Respectfully is a closing formula before the signature. An enclosure statement and a closing do different jobs: enclosed please find does not close the letter, and Respectfully does not say that a document is enclosed.

An enclosure statement and a closing do different jobs: enclosed please find does not close the letter, and Respectfully does not say that a document is enclosed.

When the cue is к настоящему письму прилагается, choose enclosed please find. When the cue is С уважением, choose Respectfully. When the English cue is enclosed please find, the retained Russian match is к настоящему письму прилагается rather than С уважением. These two source-supplied pairs support recognition of enclosure versus closing, not universal formulas for every recipient or mastery of composing a complete letter. In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

A numeric postal code and a locality perform different roles. The UPU sheet describes a six-digit Russian postcode and illustrates delivery-office coding; a displayed sample code is not a live delivery lookup. A greeting does not replace a recipient name. Recognize each requested component before trying to arrange a whole address.

г. Казань — the locality names the city. The mark and place name identify a locality, not a street or a numeric delivery code. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. provenanceRecords.shippedText: A past passive participle describes an entity affected by an action. The supplied form сде́ланный has the meaning done/made. The form напи́санный means written, and уби́тый means killed. These words describe what was done to the entity; they do not identify it as the person doing the action. provenanceRecords.shippedText: The retained examples are long past passive forms with adjective-type endings. In the shown сде́ланный and напи́санный forms, the formation contains double n; уби́тый has t. The retained source shows these forms from perfective verbs. This lesson recognizes the supplied forms; these endings alone are not a complete productive formation rule for every verb. Broader formation includes other suffix patterns and lexical restrictions, so do not manufacture an unlisted form from this small set. An imperfective past passive can exist; the supplied perfective examples are not a universal claim that every past passive must come from a perfective verb.

provenanceRecords.shippedText:
A past passive participle describes an entity affected by an action. The supplied form сде́ланный has the meaning done/made. The form напи́санный means written, and уби́тый means killed. These words describe what was done to the entity; they do not identify it as the person doing the action. The three supplied meanings differ by the underlying action. Choosing written for сде́ланный would replace doing or making with writing; choosing killed would replace it with killing.

The retained examples are long past passive forms with adjective-type endings. In the shown сде́ланный and напи́санный forms, the formation contains double n; уби́тый has t. The retained source shows these forms from perfective verbs. This lesson recognizes the supplied forms; these endings alone are not a complete productive formation rule for every verb. Broader formation includes other suffix patterns and lexical restrictions, so do not manufacture an unlisted form from this small set. An imperfective past passive can exist; the supplied perfective examples are not a universal claim that every past passive must come from a perfective verb.

The meaning written belongs to напи́санный, not to the doing/making form сде́ланный or the killing form уби́тый. The meaning killed belongs to уби́тый, not to the other two actions. The retained short form напи́сан has a single n and lacks the long adjective ending shown in напи́санный. Long versus short form is different from the action meaning: both writing forms concern writing. These checks select the action meaning of a supplied form; they do not test production of all short-form gender and number endings.

The passive form describes the letter’s state or result, rather than saying that the letter writes somebody. The short passive form in the sentence differs from the long headword напи́санный. The supplied обсужда́емый has the meaning being discussed. It describes something affected by discussion, rather than naming the person doing the discussing. The source also permits an able-to-be-discussed reading; the checked English option here is being discussed. The supporting verb form оставля́ем means we leave: it is a first-person plural present-tense form, with we performing the action, not a passive description. The infinitive оставля́ть means to leave and does not by itself name a we subject. Choose we leave for the finite form and to leave for the infinitive. The option to discuss is an infinitive meaning rather than the checked passive description. Different action meanings and grammatical functions must not be exchanged simply because forms share a stem.

The retained source illustrates the relation between the infinitive оставля́ть, the finite form оставля́ем and the present passive оставля́емый with its adjective ending. The finite we leave form is a supporting example, not itself a participle. This small set does not establish which other verbs permit a present passive or a complete formation algorithm for every verb. In the supplied leave contrast, оставля́емый is retained and оставляемы́й is rejected. In the supplied discuss contrast, обсужда́емый is retained and обсуждаемы́й is rejected. The retained accents are on the third syllable; the alternatives move them to the final syllable. Compare the accented vowel in each particular form; do not predict an unlisted form or its stress from this set. This entire session is optional and non-gating. Its present-passive stress choices belong to the optional objective, not to the required past-passive stress gate. Active-participle instruction belongs to Unit 29, not this session.

An imperfective verbal adverb describes an accompanying action. In the supplied читая письмо, он улыбался, he was reading the letter while he smiled. Reading and smiling overlap: simultaneous means during the same interval as the main predicate. The main verb places this example in the past; читая does not independently mean absolute present time. The retained examples думая and учась illustrate imperfective verbal-adverb forms. An isolated form cannot establish the tense of an absent main verb.

In читая письмо, он улыбался, The pronoun he is the explicit main-clause subject. The reader and the person smiling are the same person. The verbal adverb supplies an accompanying action by that subject, not an action by a second unrelated person. Identify the main verb and its subject before deciding who performs the accompanying action. These checks recognize timing and shared subject in the supplied construction; they do not demonstrate forming an unfamiliar verbal adverb or judging every possible literary use.

provenanceRecords.shippedText:
In Закончив письмо, Анна пошла на почту., finishing the letter is expressed by the opening verbal adverb. In Анна закончила письмо и пошла на почту., the actions are expressed by coordinated finite verbs. The adverbial opening is the bookish option and the finite coordination the ordinary option in this admitted pair. Both describe finishing before going to the post office; the register choice does not reverse those events.

The supplied Написанное письмо лежит на столе. contains a passive description and is outside this adverbial-versus-finite pair. Mere appearance in writing also does not establish this bookish classification. A verbal adverb in a different sentence needs its own contextual evidence: this pair does not license every adverbial as bookish. Recognizing the opening word is different from interpreting the whole sentence or judging an unfamiliar style.

For a compound count, inspect the last two digits first. If they are 11, 12, 13 or 14, use genitive plural for the counted noun in the basic construction. Otherwise, the final digit selects the pattern: one, two-through-four, or zero/five-through-nine. Compare 21 and 22: their final digits select different noun cases; being larger than five is not enough to choose genitive plural. двадцать два часа — двадцать два часа. две девушки — two girls.

These basic counting examples use nominative phrases. The related noun-case pattern also applies in inanimate accusative contexts, with the appropriate noun form. Other sentence cases require numeral declension as well as noun declension. A count ending in one outside the teen exception uses a nominative singular noun in the shown basic phrases. один час — один час. два часа — два часа. 

A count ending in two, three or four outside the teen exception uses a genitive singular noun in the basic construction. This is a grammatical singular form even though the count is greater than one.

Counts ending in zero or five through nine use genitive plural in the basic construction. The teen exception also uses genitive plural. Ten and sixteen therefore fit this pattern. пять часов — пять часов. двадцать один час — двадцать один час. 

For a compound count, inspect the last two digits first. If they are 11, 12, 13 or 14, use genitive plural for the counted noun in the basic construction. Otherwise, the final digit selects the pattern: one, two-through-four, or zero/five-through-nine. Compare 21 and 22: their final digits select different noun cases; being larger than five is not enough to choose genitive plural. двадцать два часа — двадцать два часа. две девушки — two girls. 

For a compound count, inspect the last two digits first. If they are 11, 12, 13 or 14, use genitive plural for the counted noun in the basic construction. Otherwise, the final digit selects the pattern: one, two-through-four, or zero/five-through-nine. All counts from 11 through19 use genitive plural here. For 15 through19 the final digit already leads to genitive plural;11 through14 override the one/two/three/four ending pattern. пять девушек — five girls. шестнадцать рублей — sixteen rubles. 

The example with 41 follows the final-one pattern and uses nominative singular for the counted noun. The example with 10 follows the zero-ending pattern and uses genitive plural. десять копеек — ten kopeks. сорок один год — forty-one years. 

The count 203 ends in 03, so final three selects genitive singular in the basic counting phrase. The count 213 ends in 13, so the teen exception selects genitive plural. пять лет — пять лет. двести три собаки — two hundred and three dogs. 

For a compound count, inspect the last two digits first. If they are 11, 12, 13 or 14, use genitive plural for the counted noun in the basic construction. Otherwise, the final digit selects the pattern: one, two-through-four, or zero/five-through-nine. Compare the supplied 203 and 213 examples and the two kopeck examples. Count value and sentence construction govern the explanation. двести тринадцать собак — two hundred and thirteen dogs. Два́дцать две копе́йки — 22 kopecks. 

The isolated table forms below illustrate genitive singular and genitive plural noun forms. They do not by themselves state a quantity or sentence context; apply the complete counted-noun rules to whole examples. Два́дцать пять копе́ек — 25 kopecks. стола́ — table.

я читал is the imperfective past option, presenting reading as activity or process. я прочитал presents the reading as a completed whole and is perfective past. A completed activity can still be described with imperfective aspect when the focus is on the process; English simple past can also translate an imperfective verb.

The retained но́вый and нов both mean new. The first is the long form and the second is the masculine singular short form. The grammatical check asks which form is shown, rather than its English gloss. Long adjectives have case, gender and number inflection; short adjectives vary for gender and number, not case. The retained examples are recognition targets, not a universal rule for producing short forms by removing endings.

In the taught modern use, short adjectives occur only in the nominative and are used predicatively to describe their subject. A long adjective can modify a noun attributively and can also be a predicate. The choice depends on the sentence, not a universal rule about one fixed word position. The following supplied forms, complete clauses and noun phrases support bounded agreement and function checks; they do not settle every long-versus-short semantic or stylistic choice.

The retained беж means beige and is an invariant colour form, unchanged for case, gender and number. Its short appearance does not make it the short counterpart of но́вый. Keep lexical meaning, inflection and adjective function separate. The correct glosses remain in Vocabulary Lab as word-meaning practice; they do not satisfy the independent adjective grammar checks.

The supplied short forms of new are нов for masculine singular, нова́ for feminine singular, но́во for neuter singular and новы́ for plural. Short adjectives agree with their subject in gender and number; they do not have a modern case paradigm. In the retained noun examples, книга is feminine singular, письмо is neuter singular, and книги has the supplied plural reading. Choose the short form for that subject rather than another form with the same lexical meaning. Some adjectives lack short forms and stress can change; these supplied forms are not a universal truncation recipe.

The complete clauses Поезд старый and Студент новый say that the train is old and the student is new. Their long adjectives predicate a property of the subject. No overt present copula appears in these supplied clauses. Long form therefore does not force attributive function, and a temporary-versus-permanent slogan does not decide every form choice. Read the whole example and its supplied meaning rather than its adjective ending alone.

The supplied новый карандаш and новое письмо mean new pencil and new letter. Each is an attributive noun phrase: the adjective modifies the head noun. These phrases alone do not assert that a pencil or letter is new in a complete clause. The adjective and noun agree in gender and number in the supplied singular examples. Do not infer an exceptionless word-position rule or every possible case from an isolated phrase. These exercises assess bounded agreement and function recognition, not unrestricted production or every long/short meaning distinction.

идти́ — to go, walk. е́хать — to go by vehicle, ride. The first describes movement on foot; the second movement by vehicle. These are different means of moving, not an aspect pair.

The table places идти́ in the unidirectional column: motion in one direction. Its other column is multidirectional, covering repeated, return or different-direction movement according to context. These directionality labels are not English verb meanings. The basic unprefixed forms in these columns are imperfective; unidirectional does not itself mean perfective or arrival.

нести́ — to carry. вести́ — to lead. везти́ — to convey, transport. Carrying on foot, leading someone and transporting by vehicle are distinct meanings. For нести́ choose to carry. A question about its meaning is different from a question about directionality.

Он пошёл к другу. — he set off toward a friend. The perfective prefixed verb presents the beginning of the journey; it does not say that he arrived. Он шёл к другу. — He went to a friend's place. This retained English rendering accompanies an imperfective form describing motion toward the friend; the Russian form alone does not specify how long he was on the way. The distractor he was already on the way for a long time adds duration that is not supplied, and he refused to go contradicts the setting-out sentence.

Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца — The boy stepped back from the stranger. The verb and the phrase after it express movement away from the stranger. There is no additional relative clause in this displayed sentence. Они у́летят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Мяч залетел на крышу дома. — The ball flew onto the roof of the house. These are different subjects and paths. The prefix contributes to the motion meaning, while the accompanying phrases identify the path and time; do not substitute a translation of a different example.

идти́ — to go, walk. е́хать — to go by vehicle, ride. The first describes movement on foot; the second movement by vehicle. These are different means of moving, not an aspect pair.

The table places идти́ in the unidirectional column: motion in one direction. Its other column is multidirectional, covering repeated, return or different-direction movement according to context. These directionality labels are not English verb meanings. The basic unprefixed forms in these columns are imperfective; unidirectional does not itself mean perfective or arrival.

нести́ — to carry. вести́ — to lead. везти́ — to convey, transport. Carrying on foot, leading someone and transporting by vehicle are distinct meanings. For нести́ choose to carry. A question about its meaning is different from a question about directionality.

Он пошёл к другу. — he set off toward a friend. The perfective prefixed verb presents the beginning of the journey; it does not say that he arrived. Он шёл к другу. — He went to a friend's place. This retained English rendering accompanies an imperfective form describing motion toward the friend; the Russian form alone does not specify how long he was on the way. The distractor he was already on the way for a long time adds duration that is not supplied, and he refused to go contradicts the setting-out sentence.

Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца — The boy stepped back from the stranger. The verb and the phrase after it express movement away from the stranger. There is no additional relative clause in this displayed sentence. Они у́летят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Мяч залетел на крышу дома. — The ball flew onto the roof of the house. These are different subjects and paths. The prefix contributes to the motion meaning, while the accompanying phrases identify the path and time; do not substitute a translation of a different example.

provenanceRecords.shippedText: Forms of который do not by themselves identify a clock question. Read the complete supplied question and its noun. Которое яблоко моё? — Which apple is mine? Asks which apple belongs to the speaker. This is the guided ownership/selection example. Которую книгу вы хотите? — Which book do you want? Asks which book the listener wants. The listener is asked to choose a book. Который час? — What time is it? Asks for the current clock time. This requests the current clock time, not which book the listener wants or which apple belongs to the speaker. The independent clock and book cues are different complete questions from the guided apple cue. These checks recognize the supplied meanings; they do not demonstrate independently asking/giving a new time or forming every interrogative. Optional repeated clock gloss practice is separate from the required checks.

один мальчик — one boy; одна девушка — one girl. For these singular counting examples, one agrees with the noun: masculine один and feminine одна. Both still mean one. Guided practice uses мальчик.

два is the form for masculine and neuter counted nouns; две is the feminine form. The supplied example две девушки — two girls uses feminine две. The following noun is genitive singular in this counting construction; the numeral choice still follows its gender.

одно животное — one animal uses neuter singular одно. одни джинсы — one [pair of] jeans uses plural одни with the plural-form noun. The plural numeral here does not mean several pairs; these are different gender/number forms of one.

одна́ and одно́ both represent 1 in the retained cardinal table. They are feminine and neuter singular forms, respectively. The existing table stress is retained; the separate counting examples are printed without added stress.

одни́ represents 1 in the supplied plural-form example, while две represents 2 with a feminine noun. Distinguish одни джинсы from две девушки by the complete supplied construction, rather than treating every plural-looking form as two.

An imperfective verbal adverb describes an accompanying action. In the supplied читая письмо, он улыбался, he was reading the letter while he smiled. Reading and smiling overlap: simultaneous means during the same interval as the main predicate. The main verb places this example in the past; читая does not independently mean absolute present time. The retained examples думая and учась illustrate imperfective verbal-adverb forms. An isolated form cannot establish the tense of an absent main verb.

In читая письмо, он улыбался, The pronoun he is the explicit main-clause subject. The reader and the person smiling are the same person. The verbal adverb supplies an accompanying action by that subject, not an action by a second unrelated person. Identify the main verb and its subject before deciding who performs the accompanying action. These checks recognize timing and shared subject in the supplied construction; they do not demonstrate forming an unfamiliar verbal adverb or judging every possible literary use.

A perfective verbal adverb normally presents an action completed before the main action in this taught construction. Anterior means earlier relative to that action. The retained сказав and научившись illustrate these forms; their labels alone do not fix an absolute past tense. Read the accompanying main predicate to establish the sentence time.

In написав письмо, она отправит его завтра, she will send the letter tomorrow after writing it. The writing precedes the future sending: anterior to a future main action is the matching description. The sentence does not require the writing to have happened before the present moment. The pronoun she names the main subject, and the writer and sender are the same person. An absolute present label loses the relative timing; assigning a different subject loses the supplied construction.

==Nouns== The accusative case is a peculiar case in Russian, as it makes a distinction that other cases do not. Specifically, if a masculine word denotes an inanimate thing ('table', 'chair', etc), then it remains the same as the nominative. If, however, a masculine word denotes a person or animal ('man', 'son', 'cow', etc), then the case uses the endings of the [[Russian/Grammar/Genitive case|''genitive case'']]. For plurals in the accusative, no matter what gender the word, they are also split: any plural word that's inanimate is identical to its [[Russian/Grammar/Nominative case|nominative plural form]], while animate plural words follow the rules for the genitive plural. Some examples highlighting this distinction are as follows: :* This chair is brown. - '''Этот ''стул'' коричневый.''' - Nominative of an inanimate noun :*I made a chair. - '''Я де́лал ''стул.''''' - Accusative of the noun :*This cat likes me. - '''''Этот кот'' любит меня.''' - Nom. of an animate noun :*I like this cat. - '''Я люблю ''этого кота.''''' - Acc. of the noun :*These women like me. - '''''Эти женщины'' любят меня.''' - Nom. of an animate, plural, feminine noun :*I like these women. - '''Я люблю ''этих женщин.''''' - Acc. of the noun So, masculine nouns denoting inanimate objects in the accusative case are the same as in the nominative case. If they're animated nouns, they follow the genitive rules, which are: add '''-а''', and replace '''-й''' and '''-ь''' with '''-я'''. Neuter nouns, regardless of animation, also keep their nominative forms in the accusative case. Feminine words are the only words to have their own accusative ending: '''-а''' becomes '''-у''', and '''-я''' becomes '''-ю'''. Feminine nouns ending in the soft sign '''-ь''' do not change. To form the plural of an inanimate word, use the nominative rules: add or replace with '''-ы''' or '''-и''', and neuter nouns change '''-o''' to '''-а''' and '''-e''' to '''-я'''. If the word is animate, regardless of gender, use the [[Russian/Grammar/Genitive case#Nouns|genitive plural]]: drop '''-а''' and '''-о''', convert or append ending consonants with '''-ов''', '''-ев''', or '''-ей''', and replace '''-я''' with '''-ь''' or '''-й'''. This summary table splits the masculine and plural forms into two sections, the left being the inanimate form, the right being the animate form. {| class="wikitable" |- ! ! colspan="2"|Masculine ! Feminine !! Neuter ! colspan="2"|Plural |- | Accusative || valign="bottom"|''As nom.'' || '''+a''', '''-я'''
''As gen.'' || valign="top"|'''у''', '''ю''', '''ь''' || '''о, е'''
''As nom.'' || '''ы, и, etc'''
''As nom.'' || '''ов, ев''', etc
''As gen.'' |} Examples: :* Dogs hate cats. - '''Собаки ненавидят котов.''' :* Cats hate dogs. - '''Коты ненавидят собак.''' :* I drove to the museum. - '''Я поехал в музей.'''

sourceCapabilities.exactSpan: most adverbs are formed by removing the adjectival suffixes "-ий" "-а" or "-е" from an adjective, and replacing them with the adverbial "-о". For example, in Ukrainian, "швидкий", "гарна", and "смачне" (fast, nice, tasty) become "швидко", "гарно", and "смачно" (quickly, nicely, tastily), while in Russian, "быстрый", "хороший" and "прекрасный" (quick, good, wonderful) become "быстро", "хорошо", "прекрасно" (quickly, well, wonderfully).

sourceCapabilities.sourceRecordId: pressbooks-traditions-grammar:Грамматика: At what time on the quarter hour
sourceCapabilities.exactSpan:
Грамматика: At what time on the quarter hour

Time Explanation and examples
At what time on the hour (0.00) Use в + accusative, but note that the number then often requires genitive case after it. In informal speech, sometimes people leave out час / часа / часов. Remember: один час; два / три / четыре часа; пять часов.

Концерт начинается в шесть часов. (18.00)
Она была дома в час. (13.00)
At what time on the quarter hour (0.15) Use в + accusative with either четверть (quarter) or пятнадцать минут. Then you use the ordinal number of the next hour in the genitive case. In essence you are saying quarter of the next hour. Note that while you can say 6:15 as “шесть пятнадцать”, in the exercises on this page we would like to focus on this other way of expressing the time.

Я приду в четверть восьмого. (7.15 – quarter of the eighth hour)
Он нам позвонил в пятнадцать минут десятого. (9.15 – 15 minutes of the tenth hour)

If you need to review the ordinal numbers up to twelve, you can find them here:
At what time on the half hour (0.30) Use в + prepositional with половина and the genitive case of the ordinal number of the next hour, or colloquially, пол_____ (genitive case of the ordinal number of the next hour). Note that the spelling of 10:30 adds a hyphen: пол-одиннадцатого.

Наш рейс уезжает в половине пятого. (4.30 – half of the fifth hour)
Мы будем свободны в полвторого. (1.30 – half of the second hour)

If you need to review the ordinal numbers up to twelve, you can find them here:
At what time on the three quarters hour (0.45) Use без + genitive with четверть or пятнадцать минут. Then you use the cardinal number of the next hour in the nominative case. In essence you are saying X hours without X minutes.

Передача начинается без четверти три. (2.45 – 3 without a quarter)
Она обычно приходит на работу без пятнадцати девять. (8.45 – 9 without 15 minutes)

sourceCapabilities.sourceRecordId: grammar20:We can read off the numbers shown on the dial. When we do so we are stating the
sourceCapabilities.exactSpan:
We can read off the numbers shown on the dial. When we do so we are stating the number of whole hours and minutes which have passed since noon or midnight. This option is always available.
In Russian we can state the number of minutes into the hour which is in progress. This makes sense up to the half hour.
We can say how many minutes remain until the little hand passes the next number on the dial. This is used after the half hour.
We can speak of quarters and halves of an hour rather than of minutes.
If the precise time is not important, then in Russian we can say things like “at the beginning of the hour” to indicate a time close to the start of the our or “at the end of the hour” for a time near its end.

The concept of the hour in progress will be unfamiliar to most English speakers. It is important to understand that “the first hour” does not mean one o'clock. It means the sixty-minute period which starts at 12 o'clock and ends at one o'clock. In the examples below the hour in progress is represented by a shaded pie slice.

The first hour began at 12 o'clock. To say that something happens at the time shown at left:
в двенадцать часов десять минут—at twelve hours ten minutes
в десять минут первого—at ten minutes of the first
в начале первого часа—at the beginning of the first hour

As the little hand passes the 1 the first hour ends and the second begins. To specify this time use any of these expressions:
в час пятнадцать минут—at [one] hour fifteen minutes
в пятнадцать минут второго—at the fifteenth minute of the second [hour]

в час двадцать пять минут—at [one] hour twenty five minutes
в двадцать пять минут второго—at twenty five minutes of the second [hour]

Once the hour is half-way done we may choose to say how soon the little hand will pass the next number. To specify the time shown at left:
в час тридцать пять минут—at [one] hour thirty five minutes
без двадцати пяти два—lacking twenty five minutes to the two

sourceCapabilities.sourceRecordId: date-russia:In [[Russia]], dates are usually written in "day month year" (DMY) order. This o
sourceCapabilities.exactSpan:
In [[Russia]], dates are usually written in "day month year" (DMY) order. This order is used in both the all-numeric date (for example "{{lang|ru|28.08.17}}") and the expanded form (for example "{{lang|ru|28 августа 2017 г.}}"); the trailing "г" is short for "года" (''goda'', "of the year"). Coincidentally, in Polish the word for year is "rok", so a similar date format is used by the Poles e.g. 1987r). Single-digit numbers for day or month may have a preceding zero (for example "{{lang|ru|28.08.2017}}") is more usual.

When saying the date, it is usually pronounced using the ordinal number of the day first (in neutral [[grammatical gender]]), then the month in [[genitive case]] (for example "{{lang|ru|Двадцать восьмое августа}}").

sourceCapabilities.sourceRecordId: grammar:forms are usual only for qualitative adjectives and adverbs. Comparative and sup
sourceCapabilities.exactSpan:
forms are usual only for qualitative adjectives and adverbs. Comparative and superlative synthetic forms are not part of the [[Linguistic paradigm|paradigm]] of original adjective but are different lexical items, since not all qualitative adjectives have them. A few adjectives have irregular forms that are declined as usual adjectives: большо́й 'big' – бо́льший 'bigger', хоро́ший 'good' – лу́чший 'better'. Most synthetically-derived comparative forms are derived by adding the suffix -е́е or -е́й to the adjective stem: кра́сный 'red' – красне́е 'redder'; these forms are difficult to distinguish from adverbs, whose comparative forms often coincide with those of their adjectival counterparts.<ref name=Belo /> Superlative synthetic forms are derived by adding the suffix -е́йш- or -а́йш- and additionally sometimes the prefix наи-, or using a special comparative form with the prefix наи-: до́брый 'kind' – добре́йший 'the kindest', большо́й 'big' – наибо́льший 'the biggest'.

An alternative is to add an adverb to the positive form of the adjective. The adverbs used for this are бо́лее 'more' / ме́нее 'less' and са́мый 'most' / наибо́лее 'most' / наиме́нее 'least': for example, до́брый 'kind' – бо́лее до́брый 'kinder' – са́мый до́брый 'the kindest'. This way is rarely used if special comparative forms exist.

sourceCapabilities.sourceRecordId: grammar:The [[conditional mood]] in Russian is formed by adding the particle бы after th
sourceCapabilities.exactSpan: The [[conditional mood]] in Russian is formed by adding the particle бы after the word which marks the supposed subject into a sentence formed like in the past tense. Thus, to say "I would (hypothetically) sleep" or "I would like to sleep", a male speaker would say я спал бы (or я бы поспа́л), while a female speaker would say я спала́ бы (or я бы поспала́).

sourceCapabilities.exactSpan:
It emphasizes the duration over which something occurs.

For example:

  • В течение урока ученики работали над проектом. – Throughout the lesson, the students worked on the project.

sourceCapabilities.exactSpan:
Note that the modifier не negates the word which comes right after it. If you were to move it in front of a different word, you would produce a different meaning. For example:

Мне не холодно.

To me it is not cold. (I am not cold.)

Не мне холодно.

It is not to me that it is cold. (I am not the one who thinks it is cold.)

sourceCapabilities.sourceRecordId: lichnoe-imya:В словообразовании уменьшительных и ласкательных форм имён участвуют разнообразн
sourceCapabilities.exactSpan:
В словообразовании уменьшительных и ласкательных форм имён участвуют разнообразные [[диминутив]]ные суффиксы (-очк-, -ечк-, -оньк-, -еньк-, -ушк-, -юшк-, -юш-, -яш-, -уш-, -ул-, -ун-, -ус-, -к-, -ик, и другие), а в качестве основ используются как основы полных имён, так и кратких форм. Например, от полной формы имени ''Мария'' и ''Марья'' образуются уменьшительные ''Марюня, Маруня, Маруся, Марюша'' и ''Марьюшка, Марьяша''; от краткой формы ''Маша → Машка, Машенька, Машуля''; от краткой формы ''Маня → Манечка, Манюся, Манюша, Маняша'' и т. п. Выбор [[диминутив]]ной формы имени зависит от полноты чувства, испытываемого говорящим по отношению к именуемому; учитывая разнообразие основ, обусловленное множеством кратких форм, и суффиксов, уменьшительные и ласкательные имена позволяют выразить в речи широкий спектр эмоциональных красок<ref name="ОРИ-5" />.

Уменьшительные имена, образованные при помощи суффикса -к-, несут в себе оттенок пренебрежения, умаления достоинства именуемого (''Сашка, Гришка, Светка'' и т. п.). Исторически это связано с существовавшей традицией использовать уже упоминавшиеся [[Полуимя|полуимена]] (которые как раз образовывались с помощью суффикса -к-) для самоуничижения при обращении к лицу из привилегированного сословия<ref group="с">Социальную сниженность, пренебрежительность подобных имён остро чувствовал [[Белинский, Виссарион Григорьевич|В. Г. Белинский]]:{{начало цитаты}}[Россия] представляет собою ужасное зрелище страны, где люди торгуют людьми, <…> страны, где люди сами себя называют не именами, а кличками: Ваньками, Стешками, Васьками, Палашками.{{конец цитаты|источник=[[s:Письмо Н. В. Гоголю (Белинский)|В. Г. Белинский. «Письмо Н. В. Гоголю»]]}}</ref>. Однако среди простого народа при общении равных по социальному положению людей эта форма имён, как правило, не имела такого оттенка, свидетельствуя лишь о простоте обращения и очевидной близости. Тем не менее в современном [[Русский язык|русском языке]] [[диминутив]]ные имена наподобие ''Васька, Маринка, Алка'' считаются стилистически приниженными

Есть полные имена — Ирина, Евгения, Александр и др., сокращённые или краткие имена — Ира, Женя, Саша и др., а также уменьшительно-ласкательные — Ирочка, Женечка, Сашенька и др.
